body:
Same class as #3040. `fold_warnings_located` (`crates/ui/src/operations.rs`) groups warnings by a numeric key, and a group prints only the line of its first warning. `Warning::AvoidHit { part, .. }` uses `216 + part`, so the range is 216..=220. `Warning::UndercutLift` (Slot Undercut, commit 5452810e5, 2026-11-19) uses **217**, the key of an `AvoidHit` on part 1. When the undercut lift comes first, the blocking "Do not touch" hit on part 1 folds into the advisory as "repeated on N more moves" and is not shown.

#3040 / PR #3062 moves `DrillUndersize` from 216 to 223 and expected `UndercutLift` at 222 (PR #2836's plan). Keys in use on main: 221 is `FirstTraverseLow` and 224 is `FirstTraverseUnderTable`, so 222 is free.

Done means: `UndercutLift` folds under a key outside 216..=220 that no other warning uses (222), and a pinning test folds one `UndercutLift` and one `AvoidHit` on part 1 and asserts both lines are shown, like `a_drill_undersize_never_hides_an_avoid_hit` in #3062.

Since PR #3185, the post-merge gate runs one independent run for each merge commit. Several gates now run at the same time. Three runs failed with the same signature: a UI test binary stops in 0-2 s with `exit -1`. The log shows no test output, no panic and no assert. Later runs of the same code pass the same step.

| Run | Commit | Runner | Red step | Gate job time (UTC) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 44948384882 | 273642212 | skull | `ui suites: lib` | 20:50-22:15 |
| 44950073227 | 6ffa808ae | egg | `ui suites: trace_parity` | 21:09-22:08 |
| 44955923206 | ced4dc34e | wopr | `ui suites: egui_app` | 22:16-22:38 |

Evidence from the jobs API:
- wopr and wopr-2 look like two runners on one host. The red run on wopr (22:16-22:38) overlapped the run on wopr-2 for a0fe9f1dc (22:07-22:33).
- The host of skull, egg, len-pm, dude and cheese is not known from the API.

1. Serialize the UI suites on one host: one concurrency group for each host, or a host lock around the UI suites steps.
2. Find the shared resource and give each run its own copy.

This is not on the cut list of v0.25.0. The release gate runs on `cut.yml`; it uses a re-run of the failed step for this signature.

body:
`cut.yml` runs both its jobs on `runs-on: [self-hosted, linux]`. GitHub matches labels case-insensitively, and every post-merge runner is registered with `self-hosted,Linux,X64,camcraft-post-merge`. Since 2026-11-21 there are eight of them. So the release gate (up to 5 h, sized for 16 cores and 64 GB) can land on any of them, including 8-thread laptops and 24 GB boxes. The PR-test runner `len` once took a cut job the same way (2026-11-14).

For the cut of 2026-11-21, a stop-gap on the runner owner's side stops every runner except `wopr` while a release PR is open.

## Change
- `.github/workflows/cut.yml`: both `runs-on: [self-hosted, linux]` become `runs-on: [self-hosted, camcraft-cut]`.
- AGENTS.md and `.claude/skills/runners/SKILL.md`: the cut runner carries the label `camcraft-cut`.

## Merge order (important)
Merge only **after** a runner has the `camcraft-cut` label: Settings -> Actions -> Runners -> `wopr` -> add label `camcraft-cut` (optionally `uma` as a backup). No re-registration is needed. If `cut.yml` asks for the label before any runner has it, the gate waits in the queue forever. Never merge it during a cut.

Done means: `cut.yml` targets `camcraft-cut`, the docs name it, at least one runner carries the label, and the next cut's gate runs there.

title: STEP import removes a short edge from a Fusion solid and then refuses the enlarged gap

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happens

CamCraft refuses a Fusion STEP model of a heater block. The user reproduced the failure in the desktop app on macOS (v0.24.0, commit `e6e04f5d0`). The MCP tool `import_model` gives the same result. Two AP214 exports and one AP242 export contain the same edge geometry. All three give this diagnostic:

```text
import_model: corrupt STEP: solidcore: import_step produced an invalid result: 1 of 1 solid item(s) refused; first #14 at check: a vertex sits 1.157e-2 mm off its edges (limit 1e-3) - re-export the model, or import an STL
```

The user can view an STL copy. A STEP copy exported from FreeCAD gives the same gap. The original CAD files stay local.

### Where the gap comes from

A diagnostic probe built the same STEP record twice with the pinned Solidcore version (`2016386`). Only the healing setting changed.

| Measurement | Before healing | After normal import healing |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Edges in the solid | 999 | 998 |
| Gap at the start of spline edge `#3375` | 0.006223 mm | 0.011573 mm |
| Largest vertex-to-endpoint gap in the solid | 0.007736 mm | 0.011573 mm |

The file defines edge `#3407` between vertices `#2564` and `#2120`. The vertices are 0.009944 mm apart. Spline edge `#3375` starts at `#2564`. Healing removes `#3407` and redirects `#3375` to `#2120`. Measuring from that vertex to the same spline endpoint reproduces the reported gap. The diagnostic names the solid (`#14`), so the user cannot identify the affected edge.

FreeCAD (Open CASCADE) keeps both vertices and all 999 edges. It reports one valid, closed solid with 345 faces. The file declares 0.010 mm uncertainty.

### Two limits still apply

The largest gap before healing already exceeds CamCraft's fixed 0.001 mm vertex limit. A separate probe passed the reader's record to the machining mesher at the normal 0.005 mm chord target. The mesher refused face 0 with a measured deviation of 0.011141 mm. Increasing the vertex limit alone would still leave a mesh refusal.

### Decision requested

Can the importer preserve an explicit short edge when collapsing it increases the endpoint error on an adjacent edge? If the preserved solid still exceeds machining tolerance, should CamCraft offer a reduced-fidelity view or refuse it with the measured accuracy? Issue #2976 and PR #2994 provide a precedent for reduced fidelity on an edge-to-surface gap. This case concerns a vertex and a curve endpoint.

**Done means:** A synthetic STEP regression fixture covers two distinct vertices joined by a short edge beside a spline. The test checks the edge count and the endpoint error before and after healing. A second test pins the agreed import outcome when the source exceeds machining tolerance. The user can see which check failed and the measured gap. Machining checks continue to use the accuracy the importer achieved.

**Triage.** P3 because direct STEP import fails and an STL copy works for viewing. `effort:high` because the fix changes geometry repair and needs a regression test.

[STEP build and validation](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/e6e04f5d0/crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step.rs#L297-L337) · [Vertex limit and measurement](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/e6e04f5d0/crates/kernel/src/solidcore_import.rs#L106-L157)

A user (vibram on Discord) is cutting real parts with CamCraft on a **Mikron WF3 DCM** toolroom mill. The original Heidenhain TNC 15x control is gone: it was retrofitted with LinuxCNC 2.9, Delta ASDA-A3 servos and Beckhoff EtherCAT. The only file that fits today is the generic `linuxcnc-3axis.mch`, and its limits are wrong for this machine: Z ±100 mm and 24,000 rpm, where this machine has Z 350 mm and 3,000 rpm. So CamCraft checks the wrong travels and never refuses a spindle speed the machine can't reach.

Source: the user's public LinuxCNC config, https://github.com/paulsvc/linuxcnc-mill2-config (`mill2.ini`, README section 1), shared by the user for this purpose.

## Values (from `mill2.ini` unless noted)
- Kinematics: `trivkins coordinates=XYZ`, mm, `G21 G40 G90 G94 G97 G64 P0.025` at startup.
- X: 0 to 500 mm, max velocity 50 mm/s (3,000 mm/min), acceleration 175 mm/s².
- Y: 0 to 500 mm, max velocity 35 mm/s (2,100 mm/min), acceleration 175 mm/s².
- Z: 0 to 350 mm, max velocity 50 mm/s (3,000 mm/min), acceleration 175 mm/s².
- Spindle: ISO 40 (SK 40), analog speed command scaled 0 to 3,000 rpm; factory range 31.5 to 3,150 rpm (README). CW and CCW outputs, encoder feedback (rigid tapping possible).
- Coolant: flood only (one coolant output).
- Tools: manual tool change (`EMCIO = io`, hydraulic unclamp button), no tool changer.
- Table: 800 x 450 mm (README).
- Post: `linuxcnc.cps`.

## Done means
- A new `assets/machines/mikron-wf3-dcm-linuxcnc.mch` with the values above:
  - travels from the ini limits;
  - spindle max 3,000 rpm;
  - flood coolant only;
  - manual tool change;
  - the LinuxCNC post;
  - rapid and feed limits from the max velocities.
- A machine-file test pins the travels, the spindle limit and the post name, and checks that a 3,500 rpm operation is refused (or warned) on this machine, the same way the other shipped machines are tested.
- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` lists it.

body:
Research only: no code, no branch, no PR, no lane slot (AGENTS.md "needs-research is research, not code").

## Why
CamCraft ships 48 machine files (`assets/machines/*.mch`), but the simulation shows each machine as simple blocks and cylinders (#2584). Many machine makers publish real 3D models of their machines, so the posed machine could look like the actual machine.

## Questions to answer (in comments on this issue)
1. **Which machines have a public 3D model?** For each `.mch` file, list: the maker's page, the format (STEP, Parasolid, IGES, STL...), whether the model is split into moving parts (table, saddle, head, spindle, rotary axes) or is one solid, its size, and the **licence or terms of use**.
   Machines: 3axis-vmc, agiecut-classic-2s, doosan-dnm(-3axis), fehlmann-picomax55, grbl-3axis, grblhal-3axis, haas-dm1, haas-dt1, haas-mini-mill, haas-vf2, haas-vf2ss, lathe, linuxcnc-3axis, makera-carvera(-air), makera-z1, millturn, sienci-altmill-2x4/4x4/4x8, sinker-edm, sodick-alc400g, tilthead, tinyg-3axis, the Tormach range (440, 770/770M/770M+/770MX/-ML/microarc4, 1100 S1-S3/M/M+/MX, 1300PL, 1500MX, 8L, 15L/15LX Slant-Pro, 24R, xsTECH/Pro), vmc. Generic files (vmc, 3axis-vmc, lathe, millturn, tilthead, the grbl/tinyg/linuxcnc ones) need no vendor model; say so.
2. **Download** each model that may be downloaded for local use into `~/m5data/machine-cad/<machine>/` on M5, with a `SOURCE.md` per machine: the URL, the date, the licence text or a link to it, and the file's sha256. **Never commit them to this repo or rehost them anywhere** unless the licence clearly allows redistribution. Do not download anything behind a login or sign-up form; list it as "needs a human" instead.
3. **Can CamCraft show them?** Check each model against what the sim view needs:
   - Can its parts be mapped to the `.mch` axis tree (which part moves with X, Y, Z, A, B, C)?
   - How many triangles does each part have after meshing at display resolution? Is decimation needed?
   - Where is its origin compared with the `.mch` machine zero?
4. **Where it should live.** Pick one, with the reasons:
   - (a) in CamCraft: a STEP or mesh body per part in the `.mch` file (#2591), loaded from a path the user supplies, since the model itself is not ours to ship;
   - (b) a side project: a fetch script plus per-machine part maps in `mkinney/cam-tools-and-fixtures` (the same pattern as its vendor fixture fetch), which CamCraft reads when present;
   - (c) URDF assemblies (#2593), for example built in SolidCraft from the vendor STEP.

## Clean-room limits
Use machine makers' own public downloads only. **No models from Autodesk, Fusion, HSMWorks or any other CAM vendor's machine library**, and nothing taken from another CAM product's install.

## Done means
- One comment per machine family with the table from question 1.
- The models that may be downloaded are in `~/m5data/machine-cad/`, each with its `SOURCE.md`.
- A recorded decision on (a), (b) or (c).
- The concrete sub-issues for that decision are filed, each with one `P*`, one `effort:*`, `area:*`, `source:agent`, "Part of #this" and a "Done means" line. This issue is then closed.

Related: #2584 (simple machine model), #2591 (STEP body in .mch), #2593 (machine from URDF), #2587 (sim view).

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## Need

2D Chamfer currently cuts the full requested chamfer in one pass.

The operation calculates the final depth from the requested width and angle. It then runs the selected closed or open path at that one depth.

A single pass can apply a large cutting load to a chamfer mill. It can also reduce finish quality on a deep chamfer or on a difficult material.

Users need to distribute the chamfer over several progressive passes:

- The first pass makes a small chamfer.
- Later passes increase the chamfer width.
- The final pass reaches the authored width.
- The final part geometry remains unchanged.

This feature must not create several parallel paths at the same depth. Each pass must advance to a larger chamfer width and its matching derived depth.

## Meaning of passes

In this issue, **passes** means progressive chamfer passes across the width.

It does not mean generic Z stepdown. The Chamfer depth comes from the horizontal width and the cone angle. A separate Z stepdown could break the required cone-to-face contact.

It does not model physical tool-tip diameter, flat length, or radius. That work belongs to #895.

## Current behavior

- `ChamferParams` holds one final `width`.
- The generator derives one `break_depth` from `width * tan(angle)`.
- The generator derives one virtual-tip Z.
- The motion uses one Z level.
- 2D Chamfer has no **Passes** tab.
- The operation records one `EdgeBreak`.
- A one-pass path defines the current compatibility output.

## Proposed user interface

Show the **Passes** tab for 2D Chamfer.

Add one field:

| Field | Default | Range | Meaning |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Number of passes | 1 | 1–100 | The number of progressive chamfer passes |

Tooltip:

> The operation cuts progressive chamfer widths from the first pass to the final pass. The final pass creates the complete requested width.

A value of `1` keeps the current behavior.

Do not add a raw Z stepdown field. The user controls the final width and the pass count. The generator derives each pass depth.

## Pass-width rule

Let:

- `w` be the final authored chamfer width.
- `n` be the number of passes.
- `i` be the current pass number, starting at 1.
- `a` be the chamfer angle in degrees.
- `r` be the tip offset from #3153.

Each pass uses:

```text
pass width i = w × i / n
```

For a final width of `2 mm` and two passes:

```text
pass 1 width = 1 mm
pass 2 width = 2 mm
```

For four passes:

```text
0.5 mm
1.0 mm
1.5 mm
2.0 mm
```

The sequence always starts at the smallest width and ends at the final width.

## Depth rule

The final authored break depth remains:

```text
final depth = w × tan(a)
```

Each progressive pass uses:

```text
pass depth i = pass width i × tan(a)
```

The virtual cone-tip Z for each pass is:

```text
tip Z i = Top Z - (r + pass width i) × tan(a)
```

The tip offset stays constant through the sequence.

The operation changes the cone depth for each pass. It does not move the cutter axis farther from the selected edge on each pass.

## Pass transition

The base implementation uses a safe retract between passes.

Each pass follows this order:

1. Enter on the air side.
2. Cut the complete selected path at the pass depth.
3. Leave on the air side.
4. Retract to the retract or clearance plane.
5. Move to the next pass.
6. Enter at the next progressive depth.

The operation must not plunge directly from one chamfer depth to the next.

The lead rules from #3237 apply to each pass when that issue is available. Before #3237, the implementation must preserve the safe open-chain approach and exit from #2988.

## Closed-path rule

For a closed path:

- Passes run from the shallowest width to the final width.
- Each pass follows the selected climb direction.
- Each pass starts and ends at a valid seam.
- The operation cuts one complete loop for each pass.
- A one-pass operation keeps the exact current point order.
- Pass transitions do not create another finished edge break.

## Open-path rule

For an open chain:

- Every pass enters and exits on the physical air side.
- The final pass covers the complete selected chain.
- The cone-offset side classification remains valid at every pass depth.
- A pass that reaches model material on the air side is refused.
- A short, folded, or missing offset remains a refusal.
- The refusal names the pass and the endpoint that failed.

## Edge-break rule

Only the final pass represents the finished authored chamfer.

Record one `EdgeBreak` for each selected source path:

- The edge remains the original selected edge.
- The width remains the authored final width.
- The depth remains `w × tan(a)`.
- The slope remains `tan(a)`.
- Intermediate passes do not receive separate `EdgeBreak` records.

Stock simulation and collision checks still evaluate every generated pass motion.

This rule prevents intermediate roughing passes from receiving full finished-chamfer credit.

## Tool and safety checks

The final pass must pass the existing checks:

- The tool must be a supported chamfer mill.
- The operation angle must match the tool cone.
- The active tool radius must cover `r + w`.
- The tool flute reach must cover `(r + w) × tan(a)`.
- Every pass width must be finite, positive, and increasing.
- The cone envelope must stay safe for every pass.
- Every retract and pass transition must remain clear of the model.

The implementation may use the final pass for monotonic radius and flute-reach limits. It must still verify the actual swept motion of every pass.

The implementation must refuse:

- A pass count outside 1–100.
- More levels than the shared maximum-pass budget allows.
- Non-finite calculated widths or depths.
- A pass transition that enters model material.
- An air-side cone sweep that reaches model material.

The diagnostic must name the selected chain, pass number, conflict location, and safe correction.

## Feed behavior

Each progressive pass uses the Chamfer cutting feed.

This issue does not add:

- A roughing feed.
- A finishing feed.
- A feed reduction for the first pass.
- A separate feed for pass links.

## Proposed fix

1. Add a pass count to the 2D Chamfer operation parameters.
2. Add the pass count to the project parameter DTO.
3. Add the pass count to MCP operation create, edit, read, and job-description output.
4. Show the field on the 2D Chamfer **Passes** tab.
5. Generate cumulative widths from the first pass to the final pass.
6. Derive each pass depth from width and angle.
7. Derive each virtual-tip Z from tip offset and pass width.
8. Run the passes from the shallowest to the deepest.
9. Retract safely between passes.
10. Apply the lead rule from #3237 to each pass.
11. Keep one final `EdgeBreak` for each selected source path.
12. Reuse shared level or pass machinery only when its transition assumptions match Chamfer.
13. Update the operation guide, field help, and examples.

#1890 and PR #3220 provide prior art for progressive 3D Deburr passes. The 2D Chamfer implementation must use its own cone geometry, width law, and `EdgeBreak` law.

## Compatibility

A pass count of `1` must preserve:

- Point order.
- Z level.
- Entry and exit motion.
- Retract structure.
- Notes.
- `EdgeBreak` values.
- Existing CL and G-code goldens.

Old projects must read an absent pass count as `1`.

The default value must not add extra project JSON or digest bytes. Old readers must reject a project with more than one pass after the project-format version changes.

New readers must load old one-pass projects.

## Out of scope

This issue does not add:

- Generic Chamfer stepdown.
- Constant-depth Chamfer mode.
- Stock to leave.
- Different roughing and finishing feed rates.
- Spring passes.
- Flat-tip, ball-tip, or radiused chamfer tools.
- Per-pass tip offset.
- User-selectable level or pass links.

## Dependencies

- #2988 and PR #3059 define selected open chains.
- #3153 defines tip offset.
- #3237 defines lead-in and lead-out.
- #895 defines real physical chamfer-tip geometry.

The implementation should complete after #2988 and #3153. It should reuse #3237 for safe entry and exit when #3237 is available.

## Required tests

Add tests that prove:

- One pass is byte-equivalent to the current path.
- Two passes create increasing widths.
- A 45-degree, 2 mm final chamfer uses 1 mm and 2 mm pass widths.
- A 45-degree, four-pass chamfer uses evenly spaced progressive widths.
- Each pass depth equals `pass width × tan(angle)`.
- Each virtual-tip depth includes tip offset.
- Passes run from shallow to final depth.
- A transition retracts safely between passes.
- A closed path cuts every progressive pass once.
- An open chain enters and exits safely for every pass.
- #3237 lead settings apply to every pass.
- Only the final pass produces the finished `EdgeBreak`.
- Intermediate motion remains included in simulation and collision checks.
- Pass counts below 1 and above 100 are refused.
- The shared maximum-pass limit is enforced.
- The tool-radius refusal names the final limiting pass.
- The flute-reach refusal names the final limiting pass.
- Old projects read pass count as 1.
- A default project round-trip keeps the old bytes.
- MCP can create, edit, and read the pass count.
- The UI shows the field and tooltip.
- The guide describes the progressive-width and depth rules.

## Done means

- 2D Chamfer shows a **Passes** tab.
- The user can select 1–100 progressive passes.
- The final pass reaches the authored chamfer width.
- Each pass depth follows the chamfer angle.
- Each virtual-tip depth follows the tip offset.
- The operation runs from the shallowest to the final pass.
- Transitions retract safely between passes.
- One pass preserves the current output.
- Only the final pass records a finished edge break.
- Focused motion, app, UI, MCP, project, and simulation tests pass.
- The reached heavy lanes run on the final branch.
- The site guide documents the pass-width law.

Changelog: Add progressive passes to 2D Chamfer while preserving the final requested chamfer width.

title: 2D Chamfer: add configurable lead-in and lead-out

labels.name: enhancement

body:
## Need

2D Chamfer has no user control for lead-in or lead-out.

The operation lowers the tool at the first cut point and starts the chamfer immediately. This behavior can place the tool directly on a finished edge. It can also create visible tool marks at the start or end of a chamfer.

Open-chain support from #2988 adds a fixed air-side extension at each endpoint. That extension has no user-selected shape, length, radius, or feed behavior. It is not a complete lead feature.

Users need to:

- Start and finish a chamfer away from the final edge.
- Select a lead shape that fits the available air space.
- Use a tangential entry when a direct or perpendicular entry leaves a mark.
- Use a different lead-out when the end of the path has different clearance.
- Shorten a lead near a wall, fixture, or nearby part.
- Use the same lead concepts that 2D Contour already provides.

This issue separates three motions:

1. **Entry** moves in Z from a safe plane to the lead start.
2. **Lead-in** moves in XY and joins the chamfer path.
3. **Lead-out** moves in XY and leaves the chamfer path.

This issue adds lead-in and lead-out. It does not add ramp or helical entry.

## Current behavior

- `ChamferParams` has no lead-in or lead-out values.
- 2D Chamfer has no **Lead in / Lead out** tab.
- Closed paths enter at the selected seam and cut one circuit.
- Open paths receive fixed air-side extensions from #2988.
- The operation runs one chamfer path at one derived depth.
- The lead geometry is not persisted, exposed through MCP, or documented.

The 2D Contour lead model in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_params.rs` is useful prior art. Its `Lead` values are:

- `None`
- `Linear`
- `Arc`
- `Tangential`
- `Perpendicular`

Contour lead-fit logic also shrinks a lead when the requested shape does not fit. Chamfer needs stricter checks because the chamfer cone, not only a cutter centerline, moves through the lead.

## Proposed user interface

Show the **Lead in / Lead out** tab for 2D Chamfer.

Add these lead-in choices:

| Type | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| None | None | Start directly on the path. |
| Linear | Length | Enter behind the path tangent. |
| Arc | Radius | Join the path with a quarter arc. |
| Tangential | Radius | Join the path with a tangential semicircle. |
| Perpendicular | Length | Enter from the normal direction. |

Add these lead-out choices:

- Same as lead-in
- None
- Linear
- Arc
- Tangential
- Perpendicular

Show only the length or radius that the selected lead uses.

Use these defaults:

- Lead-in: `None`
- Lead-out: `Same as lead-in`

Old projects with no lead fields must read as `Lead::None`. A default operation must preserve the existing path.

## Motion order

The motion order for one selected chain is:

1. Rapid to the lead-start point.
2. Move in Z to the chamfer depth with the existing entry law.
3. Feed through the lead-in.
4. Cut the complete selected chamfer path.
5. Feed through the lead-out.
6. Retract to a safe plane.
7. Move to the next chain or finish the operation.

The chamfer cutting feed controls each lead feed. This issue does not add a separate lead feed.

## Closed-path rule

For a closed path:

- Lead-in starts on the air side at the selected seam.
- Lead-in joins the path at the seam.
- The operation runs the closed path once.
- Lead-out leaves from the same seam.
- The planner must prevent the lead-in and lead-out from crossing.
- The operation records the selected edge break once.

## Open-path rule

For an open chain:

- Lead-in and lead-out follow the physical air side at each endpoint.
- The planner reads the material side from the selected model.
- The planner does not infer the air side only from chain point order.
- Explicit `Side` must agree with the physical wall class.
- The fixed extension from #2988 moves under the new lead planner.
- A user selection of `None` adds no extra XY feed motion.
- A sharp turn near an endpoint must not receive an unsafe generic extension.

## Lead-fit rule

The implementation follows this order:

1. Build the requested lead.
2. Verify the complete cutter-cone sweep.
3. If the lead does not fit, halve its length or radius up to the existing lead-fit limit.
4. If a smaller lead fits, report the requested and used values in the operation notes.
5. If no safe lead fits, refuse the operation.

The operation must not silently replace an unsafe requested lead with `None`.

The refusal must name:

- The lead-in or lead-out that failed.
- The selected chain.
- The conflict location.
- The unavailable air space or material conflict.
- A useful correction, such as a shorter lead or a smaller radius.

## Cone safety rule

The lead check must verify the complete active cone envelope. It must not verify only the centerline or the virtual tip.

The check must include:

- Chamfer width.
- Cone angle.
- Tip offset from #3153.
- The full active cone band.
- The cutter body above the cone.
- The lead-to-path transition.
- The complete line or arc sweep.

A lead is legal only when that complete sweep stays on the air side and outside the model.

The generated lead must not:

- Cross selected model material.
- Enter through a finished face.
- Pass through another selected chain.
- Fold onto itself.
- Add finished geometry outside the selected edge.
- Add `EdgeBreak` credit.

## Proposed fix

1. Add persistent lead-in and lead-out values to the 2D Chamfer parameter model.
2. Reuse the existing `Lead` value family where the semantics match.
3. Add a Chamfer-specific lead planner.
4. Reuse Contour shape construction only where the mathematics match.
5. Derive the physical air side from the selected open or closed model boundary.
6. Sweep the complete cutter cone through every lead move.
7. Keep the existing Chamfer path when both leads use `None`.
8. Add the fields to project serialization and version migration.
9. Add the fields to MCP create, edit, read, and job-description output.
10. Show the controls in the 2D Chamfer **Lead in / Lead out** tab.
11. Update the operation guide and field help.

The implementation must not copy the Contour centerline room check and call it sufficient for Chamfer.

## Compatibility

- A default 2D Chamfer keeps the current closed-loop output.
- Old projects read absent lead fields as `None`.
- Old readers must reject non-default lead settings after the project-format version change.
- A `None` default must not add extra project JSON or digest bytes.
- The lead values must round-trip through project save and load.
- The lead values must round-trip through MCP.

## Related work

- #2988 and PR #3059 add selected open chains.
- #3153 adds tip offset.
- #895 models real flat, ball, or radiused chamfer-tool tips.
- #3132 and PR #3140 address a 2D Contour lead issue and remain separate.

This work must use the final chain and cone geometry from #2988 and #3153.

## Required tests

Add tests that prove:

- A closed-loop path with `None` remains unchanged.
- Missing project fields read as `None`.
- Every lead shape produces the expected geometry.
- Lead-out can differ from lead-in.
- Lead direction follows the climb direction.
- A closed path uses the correct seam for both leads.
- Open-chain leads stay on the physical air side.
- A positive tip offset remains safe through the transition.
- An inside wall does not receive an outward lead.
- A self-crossing lead is refused.
- A material-crossing lead is refused.
- A lead that can fit only when smaller is shrunk and reported.
- A lead that cannot fit is refused.
- A lead adds no `EdgeBreak` credit.
- UI values round-trip through the operation.
- Project values round-trip through save and load.
- MCP can create, edit, and read each lead value.

## Out of scope

This issue does not add:

- Ramp or helical entry.
- A separate lead feed.
- User-selected retract or pass links.
- Multiple Chamfer passes.
- Real tool-tip radius or diameter.
- Stock-to-leave or finishing stock.

## Done means

- 2D Chamfer shows lead-in and lead-out controls.
- All supported lead shapes generate deterministic motion.
- Open and closed paths use the physical air side.
- The complete cutter cone stays safe through every lead.
- Default and old projects preserve the previous path.
- No safe room produces an explicit refusal.
- Lead motion adds no `EdgeBreak` credit.
- Motion, app, UI, MCP, project, and simulation tests pass.
- The site guide describes the new controls.

Changelog: Add configurable lead-in and lead-out moves to 2D Chamfer.

body:
A small, separate slice of the post-merge work. #2908 (lanes, claimed by the maintainer) stays as it is. Proposed in the mkinney comments on #2908 of 2026-11-21.

## What happens now

`post-merge.yml` uses one concurrency group for `main` (`post-merge-main`, `cancel-in-progress: false`). One run at a time; a second push waits, and a third push cancels the waiting one. A merge batch costs cancelled runs, and a red run covers several merges, so finding the breaking merge needs a bisect (#3111 took hours).

## Wanted

1. One concurrency group per commit: `post-merge-${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }}`, `cancel-in-progress: false`. Each push runs on its own free `camcraft-post-merge` runner and always finishes; nothing waits behind another run and nothing is cancelled. The `gate` job does not change. With today's two runners (wopr, uma) two merges are gated at once; more runners only add capacity.
2. Results can now finish out of order. The `report` job gets its own concurrency group (`post-merge-report`, `cancel-in-progress: false`) and a full-history checkout. `.github/scripts/post-merge-report.sh` keeps the last reported commit in a hidden marker in the rolling issue body (`<!-- post-merge-last-sha: <sha> -->`) and skips (notice only) a run whose commit is an ancestor of that sha and not equal to it (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`). No new secrets or repository variables.
3. An xtask test (like `xtask/tests/post_merge_report.rs`) pins: the per-commit group, `cancel-in-progress: false`, and the report skipping an older commit.

This is a workflow change: the maintainer decides (the review labels it `needs-maintainer`).

Done means: two pushes in a row each get a full post-merge run that finishes (neither is cancelled); a red run names exactly its own commit; an older green run never closes the rolling issue that a newer red run opened (pinned by the xtask test).

title: 2D Chamfer: select a tip offset

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## Wanted

A 2D Chamfer can state a tip offset. The cone then cuts the requested chamfer through a radial band above that radius.

This lets the user keep the selected edge and the requested chamfer width. For example, a 6 mm chamfer mill can cut a 1 mm chamfer at a 2 mm tip offset. The cutting band is then 2 mm to 3 mm from the tool axis.

## Current behaviour

CamCraft places the virtual cone tip on the selected wall. It keeps the tip at:

```text
tip_z = top_z - width * tan(angle)
```

The tool centre has no XY offset from the picked line. A larger chamfer mill therefore cuts through the smallest part of its cone. The operation has no setting that moves to a larger-radius band of the same cone.

## Proposed rule

For an ideal sharp cone, add one operation value named `Tip offset`.

```text
tip offset = r
chamfer width = w
centreline offset toward air = r
tip_z = top_z - (r + w) * tan(chamfer angle)
contact radius = r to r + w
```

For a 45-degree chamfer, a 6 mm tool, `w = 1 mm`, and `r = 2 mm`:

```text
centreline offset = 2 mm
contact radius = 2 mm to 3 mm
tip_z = top_z - 3 mm
```

The final chamfer stays 1 mm wide. The tool uses a 2 mm to 3 mm part of the cone instead of its 0 mm to 1 mm part.

The `Side` setting determines the air side for closed rings and selected open chains.

## Safety doors

- Refuse when `r` is negative or not finite.
- Refuse when the tool radius is smaller than `r + width`.
- Refuse when the cone or flute reach cannot supply `(r + width) * tan(angle)`.
- Offset closed loops and open chains with the same air-side law.
- Refuse an offset that folds, disappears, or reaches material on the air side.
- Keep the declared `EdgeBreak` on the original picked edge with the authored width and depth. The larger contact band must not create credit for more edge work.
- Stock simulation and collision verification must judge the offset cone position, not the old tip-on-wall position.

## Scope

This issue does not model or compensate for tool-tip wear. It selects a band of the current ideal sharp cone.

Issue #895 is related because it tracks real flat, ball, and radiused tip geometry. This operation-level feature can be specified independently.

## Done means

- The Geometry page exposes `Tip offset` for a 2D Chamfer.
- The value round-trips through project files and the MCP operation parameter surface.
- A 45-degree, 6 mm ideal cone cuts an authored 1 mm chamfer with a 2 mm tip offset.
- A test proves the contact radii are 2 mm and 3 mm, and the tip path is 3 mm below the top plane.
- A motion test proves a closed ring offsets toward the side `Side` names.
- A motion test proves each selected open chain offsets toward its air side.
- The tool-radius and flute-reach refusals name the missing dimension.
- Stock simulation proves the final 1 mm edge break and no gouge on the part.
- Existing 0 mm tip offset projects keep the current path byte for byte.

## Labels

Suggested triage: `enhancement`, `area:2d`, `P6`, and `effort:high`.

Changelog: A 2D Chamfer can use a selected larger-radius band of a chamfer mill while preserving the authored chamfer width.

body:
Follow-up from the review of PR #3125 (#3084), comment 7060737872.

The posed first-traverse law of PR #3125 reads the work through every pose of the work-turning rotaries. It takes each rotary line through the WCS origin, the same premise as the index-swing clause (`crates/app/src/posting_index_swing.rs` lines 28-40).

A machine file can state a `pivot` or an `offset` for a rotary. No shipped machine file does this, but a user file can. Then the line does not pass through the WCS origin, and the law reads the swept set about the wrong line. The reading can be too low, and the post is not blocked.

title: Circular: a helix entry with several rings touches the last ring's helix, and verification blocks it

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found while fixing #2898.

## What happens

A flat Circular with several rings and a helix entry gets blocking `Crossing` warnings. Verification refuses the program. The post is held. The program is refused, not unsafe.

Reproduce with the job of #2898, with entry `Helix` and `helix_radius` 1:

- center [0,0], radius 10, tool EM-0600-4FL (25 mm flutes), stepover 2, stepdown 2
- top Z20, bottom Z0, clearance Z30, stock_to_leave 0

Generation reports pairs such as `feed moves 2 and 84 cross in XY at shared depth`. Each pair is a helix arc of ring k-1 and a helix arc of ring k at the same level.

## Cause

The Circular is ring-major: each ring runs its own level ladder, with its own entry at each level. Each helix passes through its ring's start, and its centre is one helix radius inward. When the stepover is two helix radii, the helix of ring k-1 touches the helix of ring k at the start of ring k. The two helices share one depth band. The crossing law (`crates/sim/src/verify/crossing.rs`) counts a touch as a crossing.

## What was tried

The fix branch of #2898 tried the pocket's z-major order for the flat mode (all rings at one plane). That removed the crossings. But the inner rings then started with an axial plunge that was not named, also under a ramp entry. Four ramp-entry tests went red. The branch dropped that approach (`docs/decisions/2898-circular-ring-links.md`).

## Expected

The helix entry of each later ring is placed so that it does not touch the helix of the ring before it, or the parameters are refused before generation with a named cause.

## Workaround

Use the plunge or the ramp entry, or one ring only.

body:
## What is missing

We want to post a CamCraft milling job as a conversational Heidenhain Klartext (`.H`) program. Our first target is a Fehlmann Picomax 55 with an iTNC 530 running NC software `340490-03`. CamCraft already writes Heidenhain DIN/ISO programs. Issue #3095 tests that post. Issue #2227 proposes a reader for Klartext files. This proposal concerns the writer.

## Proposed design

- Add one **Heidenhain Klartext** post alongside the DIN/ISO post. Keep the implementation, machine data, and test fixtures in CamCraft.
- Let the machine definition identify the installed control, its NC software, and its tool-change procedure. Record installed options when a supported feature needs them.
- Let the post select the documented syntax for that combination. For example, the Picomax needs a manual tool change with the quill at its physical change position. Other iTNC 530 machines can have a different tool changer.
- Start with one metric setup, three linear axes, stock bounds, preset selection, straight moves, plunges, and constant-height XY arcs. Refuse unsupported operations by name. Drilling cycles, tapping, probing, and tilted planes can have separate acceptance criteria later.

## What the local prototype shows

The prototype has one output implementation. It accepts the exact model and release above. Changing only the configured release to `340490-04` or `606425-04` makes it refuse the job before writing a file.

We ran two CamCraft programs on the Heidenhain iTNC 530 programming station, NC software `606425-04 SP20`. Its converter accepted all 41 blocks of a single-tool contour and all 63 blocks of a two-tool program. Test Run reached all three and five programmed stops, respectively. Both runs reached the end of the program without a logged NC error.

This supports those two programs on the station release. Acceptance on the physical `340490-03` installation remains open. Cycle 247 does not activate the preset during Test Run. Preset activation, quill clearance, and physical coolant operation still need checks on the machine. [HEIDENHAIN manuals for NC software 340 49x-03](https://content.heidenhain.de/doku/tnc_guide/html/en/index/1242135142456/1242135142480/1242135142485/1242135142485.html)

## Questions for the maintainers

1. Should the first release require an exact NC software match? When two releases document the same feature, what evidence should let them share the same output?
2. Which facts belong in the existing machine definition, and which should CamCraft maintain for each supported control? Tool-change behavior and supported cycle parameters are the first cases we would use to check that boundary.
3. Would one bounded draft PR suit the project? We propose to rework the local prototype after agreement, then submit the machine definition, post, golden output, and refusal tests together. We can split the machine-data changes first if that is easier to review. We would include the manual references, station results, and outstanding machine checks in the PR.

**Done means:** The maintainers record whether to proceed, the first supported scope, the evidence required, and the preferred PR split. We will wait for that decision before submitting code.

- On the Stock page, the user picks Cylinder stock. The cylinder's axis always stands along Z.

What the code does today:

- `StockShape::Cylinder { diameter, height }` in `crates/geometry/src/geometry/stock.rs` builds the mesh along Z. The shape has no axis or direction field.
- The Stock page sends its rotation as a yaw-only quaternion (`quat_from_yaw` in `crates/ui/src/state.rs`). Yaw turns about Z. A cylinder is round about Z, so the field changes nothing for a cylinder. It turns a Box only.

Expected:

- The user can set the cylinder's axis to X, to Y, or to any direction between.
- The rotation field does what its label says, or its label says what it does.

Possible workaround today:

- Put a cylinder model in the document, rotate it with MoveModel, and take the stock "From model". This does not help every path: the simulation's field view refuses a stock that carries a rotation (see #2177).

What the work must decide:

- The controls: three axis angles (yaw, pitch, roll) on the Stock page, or an axis picker (Z / X / Y / custom).
- What the field view and the collision checks do with a tilted cylinder stock (#2177 closed one case of this refusal; a tilted primitive needs the same review).

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
